**Head:** `065f9b83f011fb510563443ebf52de6c7f6013ab` on `w1/W1-31b`; nothing is committed after it and the tree is clean. The DEC-655 piece is built, and `gov telemetry` now reads the exit-run session and records its version. Three packages (G, H, I) are open for you. Six cases outside the counter fail in the whole-tree run, alone too; details are under Verification.

## Built
- **No version pin.** The reader accepts any version string of two to four dotted numbers and returns the versions it read.
- **Fourth specimen's forms.** The line type `file-history-delta` and the attachment types `instructions`, `sandbox_instructions` and `silent_turn_reminder` are passed over by name and count nothing. Every other form no specimen shows stays "not measured" by name, at any version.
- **No version on any line.** The three log sources are "not measured" with the reason "a log none of whose lines names a Claude Code version".
- **A full line without a version**, or with one that is not a version number, is still refused with `SESSION_LOG_VERSION` ("names no version").
- I read the source diff line by line: it gives no figure that was not measured and drops no line silently.

## Interface as built
- **`gov telemetry` output:** the version read is in the existing `agent.version`, for example `"agent": {"harness": "Claude Code", "version": "2.1.292"}`. There is no new key and no change to the record's shape.
- **Close record:** nothing under `src/gov/close/` changed; the record carries whatever the counter returns, as before.
- **More than one version** (inside one log, or across the named sessions): `agent.version` is `"not measured"`, without a reason beside it, and the sessions are still counted. This is the interim state for package G.

## Packages (undecided; none blocks this head)
**G. Logs with more than one version.** DEC-655 says "records the version it read", singular; no case was written.
- (a) `agent.version` stays one text when all agree, each `sessions[]` entry gains its own `version`, and `agent.version` lists them when they differ (a new public key).
- (b) `agent.version` is always a sorted list (changes the shape).
- (c) More than one version is "not measured".
- As built, pending your answer: `agent.version` is `"not measured"`, the sessions are counted, and the exit code can still be 0. It is reversible in one small round.
- Why now: a ticket whose sessions span the CLI update (2.1.288 to 2.1.292, or the extension at 2.1.296) hits this.
- Recommendation (designer's, and mine): (a), medium confidence.

**H. Attachment types and line types no specimen shows.**
- (a) Keep the standing rule: "not measured" by name. This is what is pinned and built.
- (b) Pass over any non-hook attachment, counting nothing and noting how many.
- Impact: four patch versions brought three new attachment types and one new line type, so under (a) the next CLI update probably makes every log "not measured" until a new specimen is read. Under (b) a new hook-like form could be missed silently.
- Recommendation: (a) for Wave 1, with a fresh specimen at each CLI update; medium confidence.

**I. `instructions` and `sandbox_instructions` are now lines in the log.** They count nothing today (DEC-507, DEC-491). Whether they become a measured source in place of the estimate is a Wave 2 question. Recommendation: Wave 2 list; high confidence that "nothing" is right today.

## Residuals for `bootstrap.md`
- An attachment of an unseen type that carries no version is refused with "names no version", not named as an unseen type. It is on the safe side; only the reason is not the nearest one.
- When versions differ, `agent.version` says `"not measured"` with no reason; the record has no place for one (package G).
- The reduced specimen holds `file-history-delta` and the non-hook attachments by type and length only. Whether real ones carry a `version`, and what a `file-history-delta` holds, is not shown; the real measurement above did read one such session without refusal.
- The engineer read no specimen file; it built from the README and the cases.
- This worktree's first checkpoint record is numbered `CP-DAEO-6mk8-0002`; no `0001` is in the tree.
- The ORION clone sits under another session's `/tmp` scratchpad and is lost if that folder is cleaned.
- The six failures above that fail alone (W1-33, W1-48, W1-49).
